example.title: Putnam County Bridge No. 111 (Dills Ford Bridge), County Road 50 over Little Walnut Creek

brief: Two-span Daniel Luten filled-spandrel reinforced-concrete arch, 170 ft overall with two low, flat elliptical arches of about 81 ft each, a narrow bull-nosed centre pier with an upstream cutwater, and plain board-formed spandrel walls holding earth fill under a one-lane asphalt road. The original concrete railings were pierced with pointed-arch openings; by 1998 only stubs of solid parapet remained at the pier and abutments, the spandrels were cracking away and were strapped with short vertical I-beams on tie rods. Wooded riverbank setting with bare trees and a snowy lane on the approach (width and deck height estimated).
